children.text: A viewpoint headland on the shore of Baras, Catanduanes, where grass hills end abruptly at black rock cliffs and the Pacific spreads out before you. After crossing a stream, the walk takes only
20–30 minutes
, an easy trek that suits a dawn visit for the sunrise.
Binurong Point is a viewpoint headland on the shore of Barangay Guinsaanan, farther along the coast from Baras town on the eastern end of Catanduanes. It is about
35 km
from Virac, the island's capital, and takes
1 to 1.5 hours
by road. Low grass hills are cut off abruptly by the waves, and below them black rock drops straight into the Pacific. Travelers often compare the scene to the hills and cliffs of Batanes or Ireland.

The origin of the name is not clear, but one explanation says it comes from "binurong," an old way fishermen smoked fish over fire. There is also a story that the first settlers regarded this place as sacred. Today it is run as a community tourism site, with villagers managing the entrance and serving as guides.

From the parking area you cross a stream and climb through forest, and then the view suddenly opens up, with a ridge without a single tree stretching long toward the sea. Along the way about four viewpoints appear, and toward the end of the ridge both sides become close to sheer drops. Among the rocks there is a small pool of water, and on the rocky shore facing the sea the waves throw up white foam. With almost no shade and a strong wind, the same trail feels very different depending on the time of day and the weather.

It suits anyone who does not want a hard climb but still wants to see for themselves the sea views from the photos. It fits travelers aiming for dawn photos, surfers at Puraran Beach who want a rest day, and anyone looking to spend half a day during a trip around Catanduanes. However, there is almost no public transport and the trail can be slippery, so arrange your transport and footwear in advance.
Because the headland opens to the east, the sun rises right out of the horizon and the grass hills turn golden. It takes
20–30 minutes
from the entrance to the ridge, so it is best to set out at dawn so that you arrive before sunrise.

blocks.title: Walking the four viewpoints in turn

children.text: There are several lookout spots along the ridge, each showing the coastline from a different angle. Do not take photos at one spot and turn back; go with your guide all the way to the inner hill.

blocks.title: The narrow grass ridge at the cliff's edge

children.text: Standing at the end of the narrow ridge that reaches out to the sea, you look down on deep gaps and waves on both sides. It is a famous photo spot, but there is no railing, so on windy days do not go out to the very end.

blocks.title: Pools among the rocks and the black rock shore

children.text: Below the grass hills, among the black rocks, there is a small pool that holds water and mirrors the sky. Beyond it, on the rocky shore, you can watch waves crash and spread into white foam.

The trail starts by crossing a stream in the village, passes through woods, and then leads out onto the open grass hills. A bamboo bridge crosses the stream, and the forest section turns to mud after rain.

You register at the entrance and must be accompanied by a village guide; the guide fee is per team, so you can split it if you have companions. Because this tourism creates income for local residents, following your guide's instructions is a matter of courtesy.

blocks.title: Combining Balacay Point and Puraran Beach

children.text: Balacay Point on the same Baras coast is good for sunsets with no entrance fee and no trekking, and Puraran Beach is famous for surfing. You can fill a whole day with Binurong at dawn, the beach in the daytime and Balacay in the evening.

Cross the stream, climb the forest path and reach the ridge before sunrise
Tour the viewpoints, enjoy the sunrise and take photos, then head down before the sun gets high
Breakfast at a restaurant at Puraran Beach or in Baras town
Stop at Balacay Point or Bato Church on the way back to Virac
Take a van from Virac to Baras, check in at a Puraran Beach lodging and take a walk on the beach
Watch the sunset at Balacay Point, then have dinner at your lodging's restaurant
Call a motorbike or tricycle near your lodging and head for Guinsaanan

If surfing is your goal, stay at least 2 nights at Puraran and plan one day for surfing and one for Binurong, which is easier on your body.
Cebu Pacific flies daily from Manila to Virac Airport (VRC), taking about
1 hour
. Fares vary greatly by season, at roughly
one way, so it is worth hunting for promos. Virac Airport was heavily damaged by Super Typhoon Uwan in
November 2025
, but it has been repaired and is confirmed to be operating as of
; cancellations are frequent here, however, so check the airline's notices before you depart.
From the airport to the van terminal in town it takes about
10–15 minutes
by tricycle, around
for two people.
A van from the terminal in Virac toward Baras and Puraran takes about
1 hour
and costs about
per person. Vans run rarely at dawn, so this method alone is hard to use if you aim for sunrise, and it suits a visit that arrives during the day.
From Baras to the Guinsaanan entrance, use a motorcycle taxi or tricycle. It is about
15–30 minutes
from Puraran Beach; agree beforehand with the driver on the round-trip fare and waiting time.
Renting a motorbike in Virac for about
a day plus about
for fuel lets you move freely at dawn. The coastal road is mostly paved, but it has many curves and wet stretches, so if you lack experience it is safer to charter a car with a driver.
Day tours from Virac that combine Binurong Point and Puraran Beach start at about
per person. A vehicle, entrance fees and guide fee are included, and many depart around
and return in the afternoon. These itineraries often arrive in the middle of the day, so you cannot see the sunrise.
How to reach the island overland and by boat from Manila, with timetables, is set out in the
Catanduanes
entry. Boat trips are often cancelled by the weather, so leave some margin if you take this route.
Baras is one of the rainiest places in the Philippines, so there is no truly dry season. Even so,
March–June
, when the rain eases and the sea is calm, is the best time for walking, with the grass hills greenest and the dirt trail less muddy. In this period it can reach
in the daytime, so avoid midday visits and go up at dawn. Sunrise falls roughly between
5:15 and 6 a.m.
through the year.
August–October
is the surf season at Puraran but also the typhoon path. Typhoons forming in the Pacific brush past Catanduanes first, and just after a typhoon the roads and phone signals can be cut. From
November to January
the northeast monsoon brings much rain and rough waves, and many days the scenery is hazy. Whatever the month, check the PAGASA forecast the day before your visit.

There is hardly any lodging near Binurong Point. To see the sunrise, the easiest way is to stay a night at a surfer lodging at Puraran Beach, where a simple room costs about
a night. The long-running Majestic Puraran Beach Resort is described as the nearest resort to Binurong Point, about
15 minutes

by car. If you stay in Virac you have a wider choice of lodging, but the trip back and forth at dawn is long. Power and internet at beach lodgings can weaken at times, so charge what you need beforehand.

Before and after the trek, eat at a simple restaurant in Baras town or at Puraran Beach. Ginataan dishes, chicken, stingray or octopus stewed in coconut milk, are the signature taste here, and pancit Bato, which takes its name from Bato town, can be had for about
a plate. Freshly caught grilled fish is common, and about
is enough for a meal. There are no shops on the trail, so bring water and snacks.
Pay the entrance fee and guide fee in cash. There is no ATM in the village, so prepare plenty of cash in Virac, including small bills.
Entrance hours are listed as
4 a.m. to 4 p.m.
in some guides. To see the sunrise you must arrive at dawn, so the day before, check through the village office or your lodging whether it is possible and whether a guide will be waiting.
To see the sunrise you must leave Virac at
, so arrange the time with your driver the night before and fix the round-trip fare.
The stream crossing and forest trail become slippery after rain. Wear trekking shoes with firm soles, and if you wear sandals choose ones with straps.
There is no shade on the ridge. A hat, umbrella, water and sunscreen are essential, and it is best to avoid
9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
because of the heat.
A guide must register at the entrance and accompany you, and if your group is small it is harder to split the fee, so forming a team with other travelers from the same time slot is one option.
Records show hundreds of people a day in the high season, so to take photos in peace, climb to the ridge a little earlier than just before sunrise.
Always carry your trash out. This is a place that cares about conservation, with tree planting held here in
July 2025
at an event backed by the tourism board.
Phone signal is unstable on the ridge and coast. Download an offline map and send your last message from Virac.
Super Typhoon Uwan in
November 2025
caused heavy damage to the coastal villages of Baras, and roads in the Puraran, Agban and Salvacion areas were blocked by mud. Trip reports and tour listings from
April–May 2026

indicate that entrance fees and guides are operating, but I could not find an official reopening notice from the tourism authorities. Before you go, check road conditions and operating status with your lodging or the village office.
There is almost no railing at the cliff's edge, and the narrow ridge drops deeply on both sides. On windy days or after rain, do not go out to the end, and stay inside the warning signs.
On days with high waves, the black rock shore facing the sea can be swept by sudden big waves, so do not go down close to it.
Do not climb on days with heavy rain or typhoon warnings. The dirt trail can collapse and the stream can swell.
The midday sun is strong and heat exhaustion and heatstroke come easily. Drink plenty of water and come down at once if you feel unwell.
The coastal road back after dark has almost no lighting. Plan so that you reach your lodging before it gets dark.
Travel information for the whole island that Binurong Point belongs to. You can check boats and flights, Bato Church and the waterfalls all in one place.
A surf beach about
15–30 minutes
by car from Binurong Point, where surfers gather when waves are big and a walk along the shore is pleasant on calm days.
A sunset lookout hill on the same Baras coast with no entrance fee and no trekking needed. Puraran Beach and the small island offshore come into view at once.
A Spanish colonial-era church that is nice to stop at on the way back to Virac. You can also try pancit Bato in the town.
